- Holds worker redispatch when `WORKER_BRANCH_ORPHAN` telemetry points to a branch that no longer exists remotely.
- Holds worker redispatch when the recovered orphan branch has zero commits to preserve worker capacity and force maintainer recovery.
- Refactors the branch-orphan guard into smaller helpers so the fix passes the function-complexity regression gate.

## Root cause and systemic fix

Pulse previously treated repeated branch-orphan telemetry as a branch-specific retry signal, but it did not validate whether the named remote branch still existed or whether the recovered branch contained commits. That allowed repeated standard workers to be launched even when there was no actionable branch state to recover.

The systemic fix is to probe the remote branch and commit count before redispatch. Unrecoverable evidence now posts a clear blocker with the branch name, probe command, remote existence result, commit count, root cause, and next action.

## Files changed

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`

- Fix profile README update and screen-time scheduler plist XML escaping under Bash `patsub_replacement` so launchd commands no longer render as `apos;`, `quot;`, or `>gt;`.

title: fix: handle behind native auto-merge PRs
body:
## Summary

- Fixes native auto-merge PRs that are `MERGEABLE` but `mergeStateStatus=BEHIND` by running `gh pr update-branch` after merge gates pass and before pulse defers to GitHub auto-merge.
- Hardens server-side duplicate issue dedup by serializing same-author issue-open jobs and querying recent issues via REST instead of `gh issue list` search/index output.
- Adds regression coverage for green+behind auto-merge update-branch handling.

## Review

- Root cause for #24839/#24840 is valid: existing pulse update-branch paths handled conflicts and failed-CI drift, but an existing native auto-merge request with green required checks and `BEHIND` fell through to `_set_native_auto_merge_or_skip`, which deferred indefinitely.
- #24840 is a byte-identical duplicate of #24839 opened 9 seconds later. The dedup workflow could race because its concurrency key was per issue number and candidate discovery used `gh issue list`, which can miss just-opened issues during GitHub indexing lag.

title: fix: surface OAuth refresh failures
body:
## Summary

- Links the OAuth token-refresh failure work to issue #24954.
- Makes `oauth-pool-helper.sh refresh <provider>` return non-zero when eligible account refreshes fail, so `aidevops-token-refresh.service` can report scheduler failure instead of green status.
- Classifies OAuth refresh failures with sanitized labels such as `http_401`, `auth_invalid_grant`, and `network` without logging token values or raw response bodies.

## Context

The token-refresh timer was running, but per-account refresh failures were only warnings. Systemd saw `status=0/SUCCESS` while `token-refresh.log` contained failed renewals. The refresh helper also collapsed HTTP/auth failures into a generic network label, hiding whether the likely cause was 401/invalid grant versus connectivity.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-manage.sh` — returns non-zero when refresh output contains failed accounts.
- `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/_common.py` — sanitized HTTP/auth/network classification for token endpoint failures.
- `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/pool_ops_refresh.py` — propagates safe labels in `FAILED:` output.
- `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/pool_ops_rotate.py` — keeps rotate refresh diagnostics consistent.
- `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/tests/test_pool_ops.py`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-oauth-refresh-failure-exit.sh` — regression coverage.
